rows.label: What the project is
rows.value: The Port of Friday Harbor (Port) proposes to remove overwater piers and pilings associated with the Jackson Beach Cannery Facility (Facility). The purpose of this project is to restore ecological function of the shoreline, intertidal, and subtidal environment through the removal of creosote-treated timber over- and in-water structures. The Facility structures served pervious industrial uses that are no longer active. Creosote is known to be toxic, carcinogenic, and persistent deleterious substance present in marine environments, which results in adverse effects to fish, invertebrates, and other aquatic organisms. Removal of these structures will eliminate a source of chemical contamination to the marine ecosystem surrounding the Facility. Additionally,removal of overwater structures from shoreline, intertidal, and shallow subtidal areas will improve habitat critical for sensitive species. The existing structures degrade critical shoreline, intertidal, and shallow subtidal habitat, limiting the growth of marine vegetation, such as eelgrass (Zostera marina) and reducing the ecological productivity of these sensitive areas. Shoreline habitat is used by juvenile salmonids for foraging and rearing. Removal of these structures reestablishes natural light penetration, improves sediment conditions, and supports the long-term recovery of native shoreline and nearshore habitats.
